mutants.description: fault_time records when the converter stopped with a non-empty record (the shutdown) instead of when the first cause of the episode was captured
mutants.reason: If a cause is captured in S_SS or S_RUN and the converter then stops, fault_time holds the timestamp of the first stopped clock instead of the first cause's clock; if the converter keeps running after the cause, fault_time stays 0 until it stops.

mutants.description: A host read stamps fault_time with the read time instead of clearing it, so an empty record reports when it was last read
mutants.reason: After any host read with no new episode following it, fault_time reads as the timestamp of the read instead of 0; an empty fault_reg no longer goes with a zero fault_time.

mutants.description: Cause bit positions laid out LSB-first (OVP in bit 0, OVERCURRENT in bit 4), with the priority order misremembered as LSB highest
mutants.reason: Any recorded OVP, LATCH_ASSERT, UVLO or overcurrent cause appears in the wrong bit of fault_reg: an overcurrent window trip during S_RUN sets bit 4, which the host reads as OVP.

mutants.description: fault_reg is cleared when the converter stops, like the supervisor's window state, instead of being held until the host reads it
mutants.reason: After a fault shuts the converter down (S_RUN or S_SS to stopped), fault_reg reads back as 0 one clock later, so the cause of the shutdown is lost while fault_time still holds the episode start.

after: if(otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert || window_trip || window_trip_SS) begin
mutants.description: While running, any live cause overwrites the record with a snapshot of the currently live causes instead of OR-accumulating into it
mutants.reason: If one cause (say OTP) is captured and goes away, and a different cause (say UVLO) is then live while still in S_SS/S_RUN, fault_reg loses the OTP bit and reports only UVLO.
